whatIsCyd.title: What is a CYD?
whatIsCyd.p1: The Cheap Yellow Display (CYD) is the popular name for the ESP32-2432S028 — an all-in-one development board that combines an ESP32 microcontroller with a 2.8″ colour TFT touchscreen (240×320), resistive touch (XPT2046 or CST816 on some variants), and useful extras like an onboard RGB LED, microSD slot, and LDR. It's become a favourite in the maker and smart-home community for building compact dashboards, status displays, and control panels without wiring a separate screen.
whatIsCyd.p2: Because the display and ESP32 are on one board, you can build a full GUI device (e.g. a Home Assistant monitor) by flashing firmware and connecting to Wi‑Fi — no soldering or complex wiring required.

purpose.title: Purpose of this website
purpose.p1: This site exists to help you get the most out of your CYD when using ESPHome and (optionally) Home Assistant. Rather than editing YAML by hand, you can use the tools here to generate and customise configurations visually, then copy the result into ESPHome and flash your device.
purpose.p2: The project supports a Home Assistant monitor (sensor dashboard with clock), tailored for the CYD’s screen and GPIO layout.

atAGlance.title: CYD at a glance
atAGlance.displayPins: Display pins: TFT on HSPI (e.g. CLK 14, MOSI 13, MISO 12, CS 15, DC 2); backlight often GPIO 21 (or 27 on I2C touch variants)
atAGlance.rgbLed: Onboard RGB LED: Red GPIO 4, Green GPIO 16, Blue GPIO 17 (active low)
atAGlance.typicalUse: Typical use: ESPHome + LVGL for dashboards, clocks, sensor tiles, and custom UIs
atAGlance.note: Pinouts can vary slightly by manufacturer and revision; the config generator offers presets for common variants (SPI touch / I2C touch) and optional custom pins.

configGeneratorCta.title: Config Generator
configGeneratorCta.description: The Config Generator is a web app that lets you build your CYD configuration without touching YAML. You pick your sensors, set device and GPIO options, and get a complete ESPHome YAML file to paste into your ESPHome device. It reduces errors, keeps pinouts and substitutions consistent, and gives you a live preview of the layout. Copy the generated YAML in one click for flashing via ESPHome.

aboutCyd.title: About the CYD (Cheap Yellow Display)
aboutCyd.subtitle: A complete guide to the CYD family — variations, hardware, pinout, software stack, and references.

whatIsCyd.title: What is a CYD?
whatIsCyd.p1: The Cheap Yellow Display (CYD) is the popular community name for ESP32-based boards that combine a microcontroller with a colour TFT touchscreen in one unit. The best-known model is the ESP32-2432S028 (2.8″ screen, 240×320), but several variations exist — different screen sizes, touch technologies, and connectors. They share the same appeal: build dashboards, status displays, and control panels without wiring a separate screen.
whatIsCyd.p2: Because the display and ESP32 are on one board, you can build a full GUI device (e.g. a Home Assistant monitor) by flashing firmware and connecting to Wi‑Fi — no soldering or complex wiring required. You can <cydLink>buy a CYD on Amazon</cydLink> and be up and running the same day.

variations.title: CYD variations
variations.intro: Not all “CYD-style” boards are identical. When buying or configuring a <cydLink>CYD</cydLink>, check these aspects — they affect compatibility with cases, cables, and firmware (including this site’s config generator).

screenSize.title: Screen size and resolution
screenSize.intro: Boards are sold in different physical sizes and resolutions. Model numbers often encode size (e.g. S028 ≈ 2.8″, S035 ≈ 3.5″). Common variants:
screenSize.size24: 2.4″ — Smaller, often 240×320; some use ILI9341 or ST7789.
screenSize.size28: 2.8″ (e.g. ESP32-2432S028) — The most common “CYD”: 240×320, usually ILI9341. This project’s config generator and HAMon are designed for this size and resolution.
screenSize.size32: 3.2″ / 3.5″ — Larger panels (e.g. 320×480); may use ILI9486, ILI9488, or other drivers. Pinouts and ESPHome config differ from the 2.8″ boards.
screenSize.note: If you have a different size or resolution, you may need to adjust display dimensions and driver in ESPHome; the pinout and touch type still matter (see below).

touchType.title: Touch screen type
touchType.intro: Touch is either resistive (SPI) or capacitive (I2C). The driver and GPIOs are different, so firmware must match your board:
touchType.xpt2046: XPT2046 — Resistive touch over SPI. Shares the display’s SPI bus with a separate chip-select (e.g. GPIO 33). Backlight is often on GPIO 21. This is the “SPI touch” preset in our config generator.
touchType.cst816: CST816 — Capacitive touch over I2C (e.g. SDA 33, SCL 32). Newer/revision boards often use this. Backlight is often on GPIO 27. This is the “I2C touch” preset in our config generator.
touchType.other: Some boards use other controllers (e.g. GT911). You’ll need the correct ESPHome touch component and pinout for your specific module.
touchType.note: If touch or backlight behaves oddly, confirm whether you have the SPI (XPT2046) or I2C (CST816) variant and select the matching preset or custom pins.

displayController.title: Display controller
displayController.p: Most 2.8″ CYD boards use the ILI9341 TFT controller. Other sizes may use ST7789, ILI9488, ILI9486, or similar. In ESPHome you choose the matching display platform (e.g. ili9xxx with model: ili9341). Our generator assumes ILI9341 for the 2.8″ 240×320 layout.

usbConnector.title: USB connector
usbConnector.p: Boards are sold with Micro-USB or USB-C. USB-C is preferred for new purchases: easier cabling and many 3D-printed cases (e.g. the Aura Smart Display case) are designed for the USB-C port. Adapters (e.g. 90° USB-C) help with cable routing. Our Amazon link points to the USB-C version.

whatSiteTargets.title: What this site targets
whatSiteTargets.p: The Config Generator and HAMon firmware on this site are aimed at 2.8″ 240×320 ILI9341 boards with either XPT2046 (SPI touch) or CST816 (I2C touch). If you have a different size or display driver, you can still use the generator as a starting point and adjust the generated YAML (display model, dimensions, touch component, and pins) to match your hardware.

hardware.title: Hardware Overview
hardware.intro: The <cydLink>CYD</cydLink> integrates several components on a single PCB. The diagram below shows how the main blocks connect.
hardware.diagramCaption: ESP32 drives the display over SPI (HSPI) and reads touch via SPI (XPT2046) or I2C (CST816 depending on variant). RGB LED, microSD, and LDR are optional peripherals.

microsd.details: Optional slot for logging or assets (e.g. fonts).

ldr.name: LDR
ldr.details: Light-dependent resistor for automatic backlight dimming in software.

useCases.title: Typical Use Cases
useCases.monitor: Home Assistant monitor — Clock, date, and 6–8 entity tiles (doors, motion, energy, temperature) with colour-coded status. This site’s config generator targets this layout.
useCases.controlPanel: Smart home control panel — Buttons and switches to control lights, scenes, and automations via HA.
useCases.weather: Weather / info dashboard — Forecast, calendar, or RSS feed displayed on the CYD.
useCases.prototyping: Prototyping — LVGL demos, custom UIs, or learning ESP32 + display without separate wiring.

intro.title: 1. Introduction
intro.p1: This Privacy Policy explains how CYD HAMon Config Generator (“we”, “our”, or “the site”), operated by Element Software, collects, uses, and protects information when you visit cheapyellowdisplay.co.uk.
intro.p2: We are committed to protecting your privacy and handling any information we hold about you in accordance with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018.

infoCollect.title: 2. Information We Collect
infoCollect.intro: This site collects information in two circumstances:
infoCollect.analytics: Analytics data (with your consent): We use Google Analytics to collect anonymised usage data such as pages visited, time on site, browser type, and approximate geographic region. This data does not identify you personally.
infoCollect.personal: Personal information you provide: If you submit a contact form or otherwise provide personal information (such as your name or email address), that information is collected solely to respond to your enquiry.
infoCollect.noConsent: If you decline analytics cookies, no tracking data is collected or transmitted.

howWeUse.title: 3. How We Use Your Information
howWeUse.analytics: Analytics data is used solely to understand how the site is used and to improve the user experience. It is never used for advertising, profiling, or sold to third parties.
howWeUse.contact: Contact information is used only to respond to your enquiry and is not shared with third parties or used for marketing purposes without your explicit consent.

legalBasis.title: 4. Legal Basis for Processing
legalBasis.intro: Under UK GDPR, we rely on the following legal bases for processing personal data:
legalBasis.consent: Consent — for analytics cookies. You may withdraw consent at any time by clearing your browser’s local storage or by declining cookies on your next visit.
legalBasis.legitimate: Legitimate interests — for contact enquiries, to the extent necessary to respond to your message.

cookies.title: 5. Cookies
cookies.p1: This site uses a single first-party cookie preference stored in your browser’s local storage (cookie_consent) to remember your analytics preference.
cookies.p2: If you accept analytics cookies, Google Analytics sets its own cookies (e.g. _ga, _ga_*) to distinguish users and sessions. These cookies are governed by Google’s Privacy Policy.
cookies.p3: You can withdraw your analytics consent at any time by clearing your browser’s local storage for this site, which will cause the consent banner to reappear on your next visit.

dataSharing.title: 6. Data Sharing
dataSharing.p: We do not sell, trade, or rent your personal information to third parties. Analytics data is processed by Google LLC under a data processing agreement. Google may transfer data outside the UK; for more information, see <googlePrivacy>Google’s Privacy Policy</googlePrivacy>.

dataRetention.title: 7. Data Retention
dataRetention.p: Google Analytics data is retained for 14 months by default, after which it is automatically deleted. Any personal information provided via a contact form is retained only as long as necessary to address your enquiry and is then securely deleted.

yourRights.title: 8. Your Rights
yourRights.intro: Under UK GDPR, you have the right to:
yourRights.access: Access the personal data we hold about you
yourRights.correction: Request correction of inaccurate personal data
yourRights.erasure: Request erasure of your personal data
yourRights.restriction: Object to or restrict processing of your personal data
yourRights.withdraw: Withdraw consent at any time (where processing is based on consent)
yourRights.complain: Lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) at <ico>ico.org.uk</ico>

thirdParty.p: This site contains links to external websites (e.g. GitHub, element-software.co.uk). We are not responsible for the privacy practices of those sites and encourage you to review their privacy policies.

contact.title: 10. Contact
contact.p: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy or wish to exercise your data rights, please contact us at <email>info@cheapyellowdisplay.co.uk</email>.
